During the reporting period starting at 16:00 on May 13, 2012, a significant electrical surge was recorded within the Oakhaven Basin localized power distribution network. Telemetry data from the Regional Power Distribution Authority confirms that the energy requirements during the thermal event rose to a level exactly three times (3x) the recorded standard load profiles. The primary driver of this load disruption has been identified through high-resolution telemetry and localized sensor arrays. The surge in amperage occurred within the distribution network as a direct result of thousands of residential HVAC condensers reaching peak operation simultaneously. 

In standard operations, residential cooling units cycle through staggered activation patterns. However, the data gathered during the approximately two-hour window starting at 16:00 demonstrates a loss of load diversity, with the majority of residential condensers in the Oakhaven Basin area operating at maximum capacity concurrently. This synchronized demand created a continuous high-amperage draw across the secondary distribution feeders and substation transformers.

4. DATA ANALYSIS AND TELEMETRY VERIFICATION
The Regional Power Distribution Authority utilizes automated meter reading (AMR) and distribution automation (DA) sensors to monitor the Kilowatt (kW) consumption across the Oakhaven Basin. The following observations are noted from the recorded telemetry for the period of May 13, 2012:

- Peak Variance: The recorded peak load during the event represents a 300% increase over the baseline energy requirements.

The total Kilowatt (kW) demand remained at these elevated levels throughout the duration of the thermal peak before gradually decelerating after the 18:00 mark.
- Amperage Surge: Continuous high-amperage draw was sustained across all localized monitoring sectors, putting the distribution network under maximum thermal stress as defined by the equipment's primary operating specifications.

5. TECHNICAL EVALUATION OF LOAD DATA
The technical reporting confirms that the distribution infrastructure was subjected to a high-amperage environment necessitated by the synchronized residential load. The localized power distribution network experienced an unprecedented surge that correlates precisely with the activation of cooling infrastructure. The data confirms that the tripling of the standard load profile was not the result of industrial or commercial spikes, but specifically the simultaneous operation of HVAC condensers across the residential sector. 

No further conclusions regarding hardware longevity or external environmental drivers are included in this report. This technical operational report remains a singular record of the amperage surge and the resulting statistical anomaly in regional energy consumption data for the event on May 13, 2012.
